Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. To keep momentum on the SCCs execution and make sure we align with your procurement timeline, I wanted to capture the immediate asks and a proposed path forward.

Summary of what we discussed:
- You need a signed transfer mechanism for onward transfers from the EU/UK for our hosted inference product.
- Medisafe's legal team prefers we propose a single module selection for both EU and UK execution if possible, to simplify contract packaging.
- You expect a short DPIA scoping note and evidence pack for your internal review.

Redwood proposed next steps (we can adjust):
1) We prepare a short SCCs module recommendation memo for your legal: pros/cons and operational implications for Module options (controller-processor/processor-processor permutations).
2) Share a DPIA scoping template pre-filled with our answers to the sections relevant to transfers and data categories (PII/PHI).
3) Circulate a draft addendum for signatures (DocuSign link) once legal confirms the module choice + any redlines.

I attached a one-pager "SCCs-module-summary.pdf" and a DPIA scoping template. Can you confirm whether Medisafe wants: (A) a single module approach for both EU & UK, or (B) separate signatures/annex decisions per jurisdiction? If (A), please confirm your legal point of contact so we can route the draft directly.

Thanks — aiming to get this over to legal by end of day tomorrow if we have confirmation.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Thanks Claire — tagging the right folks internally. Quick operational note from Redwood's perspective:

- Based on the controller/processor facts Claire provided, the "processor" modules are the natural fit. For simplicity and to match your ask (single module), we recommend Module 2 (controller-to-processor flow) as the base.
- Tradeoffs: Module 2 keeps obligations concentrated on the processor (us) for security controls and audit logs, which helps your internal reviewers. However, Module 2 requires us to demonstrate stronger operational evidence (SOC 2 artifacts, retention controls for telemetry, and documented access paths).
- If Medisafe anticipates widespread onward transfers by your teams, Module 5 (processor-to-processor) or a combination can be considered, but that increases the number of executing parties and signatures.

I've attached an internal checklist of evidence we can provide quickly: SOC2 report references, retention policy extract, and a short telemetry handling statement.

Action items for Redwood ops/legal: Mina, can you confirm whether we have any technical ability to restrict telemetry collection per-customer at ingestion (to reduce DPIA risk)? If yes, that will materially lower Medisafe's concern and make Module 2 more palatable.

-Neha

Thank you for the thread. Quick legal read below:

1) Module recommendation: We agree Module 2 (controller -> processor) is the appropriate starting point given Claire's statement that Medisafe is the controller and Redwood will process patient data for inference. We'll prepare a concise legal memo that explains why Module 2 fits and lists the small number of fallback scenarios (e.g., onward transfers for model telemetry) and mitigations.

2) Redlines to expect in the draft addendum:
   - Narrowing audit window language (we'll propose a <30 day advance notice and scoped auditor list).
   - Add explicit telemetry minimization clause and an operational attestation (SOC2 + retention policy excerpt).
   - Standard carve for lawful requests from governments (we'll propose notification timing and contestability language where legally permitted).

3) DPIA scope note: We will draft a short paragraph describing how Module 2 changes the DPIA risk profile — specifically: processor obligations reduce residual risk by centralizing controls; telemetry minimization and per-tenant retention windows lower the impact score. Neha: please confirm technical feasibility to toggle telemetry collection by tenant; that will be included in the attestation.

4) Next steps: I'll circulate a 1-page legal memo + proposed redlines by EOD tomorrow and can join a 20-minute call on Friday at 9:30am BST if Medisafe legal is available. Claire, please advise availability.
